title: Type guards, narrowing and discriminated unions: retrieval check
markdown:
## Recall before you check

This retrieval pass revisits narrowing without re-teaching it. Before opening the check, say in your own words how `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in` and equality checks narrow a union in control flow; how a discriminant property with literal types drives a `switch`; what a user-defined type predicate (`value is T`) and an assertion function (`asserts value is T`) promise; and where narrowing stops: callbacks, mutable captured variables, and property access through optional chains.

## What to bring back

- A discriminated union needs one property whose type is a distinct literal in every member; narrowing on it selects the member.
- `typeof x === 'object'` still admits `null`; check `x !== null` before `in`.
- A type predicate narrows at call sites but is only as honest as its body; the compiler does not verify it.
- An assertion function throws instead of returning false and narrows the rest of the block.
- Aliased conditions (`const ok = typeof x === 'string'`) narrow when `ok` is a const and `x` is not reassigned.
- Exhaustiveness: after every case is handled, the subject is `never`; assign it in `default` to catch new members.

Answer from memory first, then read the feedback.

key_takeaways: A discriminant is a property with a distinct literal type in every union member.
Type predicates narrow at call sites but are trusted, not verified.
Narrowing is control-flow analysis inside one function and stops at callbacks.

questions.prompt: Which property makes `{ kind: 'ok'; value: number } | { kind: 'err'; message: string }` a discriminated union?
questions.explanation: kind has a distinct literal type in each member, so checking it selects the member.

questions.prompt: After `if (typeof x === 'object')`, what can `x` still be that breaks `'id' in x`?
questions.explanation: typeof null is 'object'; add x !== null before using in.
questions.learning_objective: Remember the null pitfall of typeof

questions.prompt: What does the compiler verify about `function isUser(v: unknown): v is User`?
choices: That the body checks every User property
Only that the body returns a boolean; the claim itself is trusted
That User has no optional properties
questions.correct_answer: Only that the body returns a boolean; the claim itself is trusted
questions.explanation: A type predicate is a promise the author makes; a wrong body narrows wrongly.

questions.prompt: Which construct narrows the rest of a block by throwing when the check fails?
choices: An assertion function declared with asserts v is T
questions.correct_answer: An assertion function declared with asserts v is T
questions.explanation: asserts functions narrow after the call because control continues only if they did not throw.

questions.prompt: Why does narrowing `let x: string | number` inside an `if` not apply inside a callback passed to `setTimeout`?
choices: The callback is another function and x may be reassigned before it runs
Unions cannot be narrowed in closures
questions.correct_answer: The callback is another function and x may be reassigned before it runs
questions.explanation: Control-flow narrowing does not cross function boundaries for mutable variables.
